title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)  Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)

sources.title: Cool-flame Extinction During N-Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity
A Burke-Schumann Analysis of Dual-Flame Structure Supported by a Burning Droplet

variables_studied: Droplet spacing and initial size in a binary linear array
key_findings: The primary goal of the flight experiments is to provide benchmark experimental data on bi-component droplet combustion over a wide range of initial conditions that could be used to validate numerical simulations and to develop new theoretical models.

The combustion of liquid fuels is the overwhelming energy source in the transportation sector. Insights gained from these studies can lead to more efficient and cleaner combustion technologies which are crucial for reducing pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

conditions.label: Decane droplet combustion
evidence: The chamber was filled with the appropriate atmosphere, which was varied in pressure between 0.5 atm to 3.0 atm and O2 concentration between 0.1 to 0.4 mole fraction

paper_findings.text: Cool-flame temperatures are greater than that of the hot-flame.
A dominant cool-flame, i.e., Tc > Th, is established with the fuel leakage of only 50% and relative heat of combustion of only 10%.
With the heat of combustion of the cool-flame around 20% of the hot-flame, a weak cool-flame is established when the fuel leakage is high.
